tasks.title: Strict catalogue matching
tasks.objective: Return only complete visible ideas satisfying category and explicit refinements, derived from the authoritative catalogue without padding or copied IDs. Implement the normative SPEC Matching and decision contract and the task behavior/ownership described in PLAN.md; all acceptance checks below are planned, not existing proof. Strict event aliases must denote the same celebration; legacy affinity groups such as bautizo/comunion cannot establish an actual match. Retain unrelated legacy event-helper behavior through a distinct strict predicate.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled matcher tests pass for category-only, conjunctive explicit preferences, sparse/empty, identity, motif, tone/age/gender and successive source additions/modifications without a fixed ID/category whitelist or cross-celebration alias match.
Wedding regression passes with only matching designs while literal customer-theme fidelity and independent photo helper invariants remain covered.
Existing lower-level legacy search regression passes for other consumers without becoming a fallback for active-category recommendations.

verification.purpose: Controlled matcher tests pass for category-only, conjunctive explicit preferences, sparse/empty, identity, motif, tone/age/gender and successive source additions/modifications without a fixed ID/category whitelist or cross-celebration alias match.
Wedding regression passes with only matching designs while literal customer-theme fidelity and independent photo helper invariants remain covered.
Existing lower-level legacy search regression passes for other consumers without becoming a fallback for active-category recommendations.

tasks.estimate_rationale: Uncalibrated engineering estimate: 25 minutes trace/extract shared category logic, 65 implement strict predicates/adapter, 50 controlled tests and focused regression. Queried history has unknown comparable durations/sample count; no historical median or execution budget inferred.

complexity.justification: Strict catalogue matching combines several known predicates and existing alias helpers; it needs bounded algorithm changes rather than new architecture.

scope.justification: Matching changes stay inside the guided library and its focused idea adapter and tests; the broader legacy search remains compatible.

duration.justification: The matching work estimate includes shared-helper extraction, strict predicates and controlled successive-catalogue cases; existing search scripts provide the test harness.

risk.justification: An incorrect matching predicate shows unrelated existing designs but does not itself mutate plans or prices; regression assertions expose that impact.

coupling.justification: The strict-category-matching contract supplies turn policy and response option validation in dependent tasks.

confidence.justification: Catalogue schemas, matchers and both focused baseline scripts were inspected and executed; stricter preference interpretation remains an uncalibrated estimate.
evidence: command:node --import tsx scripts/test/test-ideas-boda-guiada.ts -> exit 0 legacy baseline

tasks.title: Discovery turn decisions
tasks.objective: Resolve category discovery and partial brief changes without intercepting explicit customer actions or modifying selected designs and plans. Implement the normative SPEC Matching and decision contract and the task behavior/ownership described in PLAN.md; all acceptance checks below are planned, not existing proof. An explicit unsupported category replacement suppresses stale-category results. Emit the resolved customer-confirmed partial-brief snapshot, preserving unrelated fields, because the UI replaces its brief from result.brief.
acceptance_criteria: Turn tests pass for explicit-action precedence, partial category-only brief, latest affirmative category, negation/ambiguity, explicit unsupported replacement, retained customer preferences and resolved brief snapshot and immutable plan/selection with zero effect calls.
Existing v1 request tests accept partial briefs and retain deliberate invalid-input and explicit-action validation.

verification.purpose: Turn tests pass for explicit-action precedence, partial category-only brief, latest affirmative category, negation/ambiguity, explicit unsupported replacement, retained customer preferences and resolved brief snapshot and immutable plan/selection with zero effect calls.
Existing v1 request tests accept partial briefs and retain deliberate invalid-input and explicit-action validation.

tasks.estimate_rationale: Uncalibrated estimate: 25 minutes trace existing intent facts, 50 implement the pure decision table, 45 precedence/negative-input tests. History returned unknown comparable duration and sample count; no statistical projection claimed.

complexity.justification: Discovery precedence crosses explicit plan actions, selected ideas, direct pieces, photos and stale briefs; a wrong decision redirects the whole turn.

scope.justification: The turn policy is one new pure use case plus a focused test script consuming existing facts and matching output.

duration.justification: Turn precedence needs an explicit branch matrix and negative cases after tracing the route guards; existing contract tests supply input fixtures.

risk.justification: Wrong turn routing can interrupt edits or explicit selection; the use case is read-only and downstream integration must preserve action guards.

coupling.justification: The discovery-turn-outcome interface is consumed by response formatting and route dispatch with a common precedence contract.

confidence.justification: Existing route guards and customer fact extraction were inspected, while the new decision matrix has no comparable execution history.

tasks.estimate_rationale: Uncalibrated estimate: 20 minutes trace streaming/final sanitation, 45 formatter and instruction alignment, 45 update conflicting assertions with strict replacements. History metrics remain unknown; prose changes alone do not establish product acceptance.

complexity.justification: Response sanitation already has known streamed and final branches; a typed discovery outcome makes their strict exception explicit.

scope.justification: Presentation rules and focused regression scripts change within the guided response layer without introducing a new wire schema.

duration.justification: Response work includes instruction alignment, fragmented-stream assertions and replacement of contradictory fallback tests, using existing deterministic harnesses.

confidence.justification: Both sanitation implementations and their existing deterministic tests were inspected; new strict stream cases have not been implemented.

interfaces.title: Strict category catalogue query
inputs: Validated visible library records, customer category, optional explicit refinements, current catalogue event labels
outputs: Stable ordered actual design records, zero to six, with preserved identity and no approximate fill
invariants: Only current visible eligible records; no fixed ID/category whitelist or extra cache
Known category is required; absent refinements are unconstrained and supplied preferences are conjunctive
Source edits arrive through normal publication/build/deploy; injected successive inputs prove derivation, not runtime hot reload
Aliases equate only the same celebration; broad legacy affinity groups cannot introduce a cross-event match
integration_criteria: Category-only route and option queries call the same predicates
Thin/empty and new/modified-source cases retain their exact result membership through route integration

interfaces.title: Read-only discovery turn outcome
inputs: Validated customer messages/partial brief and existing explicit action facts
Current validated visible catalogue through IF-1
outputs: Suppressed, unknown/ambiguous, matching or empty outcome with reason, resolved partial-brief snapshot and actual design records
invariants: No plan/selection mutation and no provider calls
Latest affirmative unambiguous customer category beats stale brief; explicit action precedence wins over automatic discovery
Explicit unsupported category replacement never reuses stale category; resolved partial-brief snapshot retains unrelated confirmed fields
integration_criteria: Actual route dispatch preserves all explicit-action branches and produces category-only data in the same response
Empty and matching outcomes are authoritative and cannot be replaced by model/generic fallback

interfaces.title: Discovery response policy
inputs: Typed IF-2 outcome and customer-visible category/preferences
outputs: Short matching or honest empty text; no automatic alternative/compulsory clarification for empty
invariants: Stream chunks and final text agree on which designs exist
Suppressed turns preserve existing intentional flow text
integration_criteria: Handler uses deterministic discovery text before provider initialization
Sanitation/options and model-tool paths never turn empty into generic alternatives
